acceptance: Edits touching only metadata or small items adhere to <=2x bytes touched ratio, or a schema-4 sharded state format is introduced.
A test asserts storage ratio bounds on tiny (<200 byte) edits without requiring large descriptions.
context: Discovered during adversarial reviews (Codex, Agy, Muse) of the 0.10.0 object-store cache. Fixed per-commit Git overhead (~0.5 to 1 KiB) dominates tiny edits.
description: When task edits touch small state (e.g. title-only changes touching ~140 bytes of JSON), Git's fixed structural commit record (~0.5 to 1 KiB: commit object + commit trailers + 2 tree deltas + index.json delta + pack index entry) dominates, resulting in 3.6x to 6.4x the bytes touched. While realistic edits (~3.5 KB) meet the bound at 0.21x-0.72x, achieving <=2x universally on tiny edits requires architectural evolution: e.g. sharding index.json into subtrees (schema 4), grouping commits, or intermediate history pruning.
